_note: Timed captions and door visits. kind: sound | voice | thought. flag + flag_minutes opens a window during which interactions change (e.g. answering the door). wake: true wakes a sleeping player. The soundscape is built by subtraction: horns and sirens on day 1, gone by day 3.

events.text: You slept in your clothes. The radiator is cold. The cooler is on the kitchen table where you left it at two in the morning.
[A car horn, held down, somewhere toward Houston Street.]
[Engines idling in the street below. Nobody has come back for the cars.]
Terry called once, after the shaking: "I'm on till morning. Stay put. I'll come to you." It's morning.
[Sirens, many of them, all going east.]
[Knocking.] WALTER (through the door): "Lombardi! You alive in there?"
[Someone across the street has a transistor radio in the window, turned all the way up.]
CONCETTA (calling up the airshaft): "Nicky! You fill the tub? My Sal filled the tub in '65. Fill the tub!"
[Footsteps overhead, back and forth. Lenny in 5A, pacing.]
The sky over the East Side has gone the colour of a stop light. Nobody on the street is talking.
[Small knocks at the door.] A CHILD'S VOICE: "Trick or treat?" Then a woman, low: "Mijo, I told you, just the third floor."
Every window on the block is black. You've never seen the street this dark.
[A dog barking in a courtyard, on and on.]
[Glass breaking, a long way off. Then laughing.]
[One of the idling cars coughs, shudders and dies. The street is quieter by one engine.]
You realize you haven't heard a siren since early this morning.
[Hammering on the roof. Abe Feldman, putting his antenna back up.]
The headlights in the street have gone yellow and weak. Batteries going.
[Church bells from the parish on Sullivan Street. Sunday. They ring longer than usual.]
You can look straight at the sun. It's a dim coin behind brown haze.
No engines at all now. Just wind in the airshaft, and someone coughing.
